description: "Uses non parametric statistics to analyze size, weight, and color changes or corals grown in Mini Ocean under different lighting treatments from Summer 2024 to Spring 2025 Coral Lighting Experiment"
output: html_document

  markdown: 
    wrap: 72
---

Input: 
  `CoralColorWeightData_Rates.csv`: made as output in `MO-Wrangling-PERMANOVA.Rmd`, coral weight, surface area, and pigmentation (color) data as weekly rate of change per trial; one data point per coral per trial indicating the total change in response variable per trial
  
Output: 
  `MOStats_PERMANOVA_SingleIndependent.xlsx`: results of running a single PERMANOVA with no interactions between the independent variables. 
  
  `MOStats_PERMANOVA_SingleInteraction.xlsx`: results of running a single PERMANOVA with interactions between the independent variables. 
  
  `MOStats_PERMANOVA_Pairwise_All.xlsx`: results of Pairwise PERMANOVA tests run on Trial, Treatment, and Species separately. 
  
  `MOStats_TukeyTestResults.xlsx`: results of Tukey Test run with interactions between the independent variables. 
  

## Import Libraries
```{r import-libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(openxlsx)
library(rstatix)
library(vegan)
library(multcompView)
library(pairwiseAdonis) 
# to install pairwiseAdonis: in console run install.packages('devtools') > library(devtools) > install_github("pmartinezarbizu/pairwiseAdonis/pairwiseAdonis")
options(scipen = 9999)
# Do this to avoid a stupid useless error message
options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)  
```

## Import Data
```{r import-data}
df_rates <- read_csv("InputData/Clean/CoralData/CoralColorWeightData_Rates.csv") %>%
  # get rid of trial PBR 4 due to light timer malfunction keeping lights on continuously for 10 days
  filter(Trial != "PBR 4") %>%
  filter(Trial != "PBR 4 Control") %>%
  # add Colony 
  mutate(colony_id = str_sub(frag_id, start = 6, end = -3), .after = frag_id)
  

```

# PERMANOVAs
Run non-parametric multivariate analysis of variance (NPMANOVA), also known as permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA), using weight, surface area, and pigmentation (RGB values) as dependent variables and Treatment, Trial, and Species as independent/grouping/factor variables. For a One-Way PERMANOVA, the null hypothesis  is that the centroids of all groups being tested reside in the same place in multivariate space. A centroid is the multivariate mean position of a group of samples mapped in multidimensional space defined by a distance matrix - think of a 3D cluster or ball. We are testing to see if the clusters for all groups are in the same space (null hypothesis), or if they are in significantly different areas in space from each other (alternate hypothesis). As an omnibus test (first line of testing), rejecting the null on a one-way PERMANOVA only tells us that at least one group is significantly different. It doesn't give specifics, for example, if every level differs from every other, or if there is one level that differs from the rest.   

First we'll run a one-way PERMANOVA testing Treatment (do the weight, surface area, and pigmentation values cluster in the same space for all treatments?), then Species (do the weight, surface area, and pigmentation values cluster in the same space for all species?), then Treatment and Species (do the weight, surface area, and pigmentation values cluster in the same space for all treatments and species?). 

If we get significant differences from the one-way test, then we will run post hoc tests of pairwise PERMANOVAs and Tukey Tests. 

Note: we are using euclidean distance instead of curtis-bray distance due to having negative values in our dependent data. 

We will also need to set the seed for the number generator used within the PERMANOVA function to ensure the same sequence of pseudo-random permutations is used each time we run the code, making our results reproducible - the specific number we choose for the seed is arbitrary. We will need to do this each time before we run a PERMANOVA.

On the F Statistic: "When the F value is large, it indicates that the differences in group means are substantially greater than what could be expected due to random variation alone. Conversely, a small F value suggests that the observed differences in means are likely attributable to chance fluctuations within the groups." (<https://www.6sigma.us/six-sigma-in-focus/anova-f-value-meaning/>)

## One-Way PERMANOVAs
### Set-up
Make a dataframe holding just the dependent variables.
```{r permanova-setup}
# from <https://f-santos.gitlab.io/2020-05-07-npmanova.html>
y <- df_rates[, c("weight_g_weekly", "surface_area_cm3_weekly", "rgb_weekly")]

df_rates_test <- df_rates %>%
  mutate(person = ifelse(Trial == "PBR 1" | Trial == "PBR 2" | Trial == "PBC 1" | Trial == "PBR 1 Control" | Trial == "PBR 2 Control" | Trial == "PBC 1 Control", "Connor", "Savanna"), .after = colony_id) %>% 
  mutate(season = case_when(
    Trial == "PBR 1" ~ "Summer", 
    Trial == "PBR 1 Control" ~ "Summer", 
    Trial == "PBC 1" ~ "Summer", 
    Trial == "PBC 1 Control" ~ "Summer", 
    Trial == "PBR 2" ~ "Summer", 
    Trial == "PBR 2 Control" ~ "Summer", 
    Trial == "PBR 3" ~ "Fall", 
    Trial == "PBR 3 Control" ~ "Fall", 
    Trial == "PBC 2" ~ "Fall", 
    Trial == "PBC 2 Control" ~ "Fall", 
    Trial == "PBC 3" ~ "Winter", 
    Trial == "PBC 3 Control" ~ "Winter"
  ), .after = person) %>%
  mutate(times_used = ifelse(colony_id %in% c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6), "repeated", "single"), .after = season)

y_test <- df_rates_test[, c("weight_g_weekly", "surface_area_cm3_weekly", "rgb_weekly")]
  

```

### Test Terms Independently 
Test the effects of each factor variable on the dependent data independently of each other. 
```{r permanova-independent-terms}
# set seed for permutations so that they are reproducible 
set.seed(100)

# trial --> significant
adonis2(y ~ df_rates$Trial, 
                            method = "euclidean") 

# treatment --> significant 
adonis2(y ~ df_rates$Treatment, 
                            method = "euclidean")

# species --> significant 
adonis2(y ~ df_rates$Species, 
                            method = "euclidean")

# colony --> significant 
adonis2(y ~ df_rates$colony_id, 
                            method = "euclidean")

# person --> not significant 
adonis2(y_test ~ df_rates_test$person, 
                            method = "euclidean")


# season --> significant 
adonis2(y_test ~ df_rates_test$season, 
                            method = "euclidean")

# times used --> significant 
adonis2(y_test ~ df_rates_test$times_used, 
                            method = "euclidean")

# regress y on Species, Treatment, colony --> significant 
adonis2(y ~ df_rates$Species + df_rates$Treatment + df_rates$colony_id,
        method = "euclidean")

# regress y on Species, Trial, colony --> significant 
adonis2(y ~ df_rates$Species + df_rates$Trial + df_rates$colony_id,
        method = "euclidean")

# regress y on Species and Trial --> significant 
adonis2(y ~ df_rates$Species + df_rates$Trial,
        method = "euclidean")

# regress y on Species and Treatment --> significant 
adonis2(y ~ df_rates$Species + df_rates$Treatment,
        method = "euclidean")

# regress y on Species and colony --> significant 
adonis2(y ~ df_rates$Species + df_rates$colony_id,
        method = "euclidean")

# regress y on Treatment and colony --> significant 
adonis2(y ~ df_rates$Treatment + df_rates$colony_id,
        method = "euclidean")

# regress y on Trial and season --> significant 
adonis2(y ~ df_rates$Trial + df_rates$colony_id,
        method = "euclidean")

# regress y on Species and season --> significant 
adonis2(y_test ~ df_rates_test$Species + df_rates_test$season,
        method = "euclidean")

# regress y on Treatment and season --> significant 
adonis2(y_test ~ df_rates_test$Treatment + df_rates_test$season,
        method = "euclidean")

# regress y on Trial and season --> significant 
adonis2(y_test ~ df_rates_test$Trial + df_rates_test$season,
        method = "euclidean")

# regress y on Species and times used --> significant 
adonis2(y_test ~ df_rates_test$Species + df_rates_test$times_used,
        method = "euclidean")

# regress y on Treatment and times used --> significant 
adonis2(y_test ~ df_rates_test$Treatment + df_rates_test$times_used,
        method = "euclidean")

# regress y on Trial and times used --> significant 
adonis2(y_test ~ df_rates_test$Trial + df_rates_test$times_used,
        method = "euclidean")

# add column with row names that will print out nicely
# df_perm_independent <- perm_independent %>%
#   mutate(ModelNames = rownames(perm_independent), .before = Df)

# make excel file of results
#write.xlsx(x = df_perm_independent, file = "OutputData/StatisticsResults/MOStats_PERMANOVA_SingleIndependent.xlsx")

```


### Test Interaction Between Terms
```{r permanova-interaction-terms}
# set seed for permutations so that they are reproducible 
set.seed(100)

# regress y on Treatment, Trial, Species, colony, Treatment*Trial, Treatment*Species, Treatment*Colony, Trial*Species, Trial*colony, Species*colony --> significant 
perm_interaction <- adonis2(y ~ df_rates$Treatment * df_rates$Trial * df_rates$Species * df_rates$colony_id, 
                            method = "euclidean")


# add column with row names that will print out nicely
df_perm_interaction <- perm_interaction %>% mutate(ModelNames = rownames(perm_interaction), .before = Df)

# make excel file of results
# write.xlsx(x = df_perm_interaction, file = "OutputData/StatisticsResults/MOStats_PERMANOVA_SingleInteraction.xlsx")

```

The model of Treatment, Trial, Species, colony, Treatment X Trial, Treatment X Species, Treatment X Colony, Trial X Species, Trial X colony, Species X colony was significant. We'll move onto pairwise permanova post hoc testing.  

NOTE: Treatment*Trial was automatically removed due to high multicollinearity, meaning that the variables are very highly correlated, which makes it difficult for the model to discern their individual impacts. 

## Post Hoc Tests
### Pairwise PERMANOVAs
Next we'll perform pairwise PERMANOVAs to see exactly which groups are significantly different from each other. First we'll test Treatment, then Species, then Trial, then Colony (even though it wasn't significant in the one-way permanova, I want to see which colonies are different from each other, if any), then Treatment and Species, then Trial and Species, then Treatment and Colony, then Species and Colony, then Species and Treatment and Colony, then Species and Trial and Colony.

#### Setup
```{r pairwise-permanova-setup-1}
# R sometimes has trouble with assigning proper formats to variables so this sets it as a factor (the proper format)
df_rates$Species <- as.factor(df_rates$Species)
df_rates$Treatment <- as.factor(df_rates$Treatment)
df_rates$Trial <- as.factor(df_rates$Trial)
df_rates$colony_id <- as.factor(df_rates$colony_id)

# set up colonies as strata
# perm <- how(nperm = 999)
# setBlocks(perm) <- with(df_rates, colony_id)

# then we'll use the same y dataframe from the regular permanova step
y <- df_rates[, c("weight_g_weekly", "surface_area_cm3_weekly", "rgb_weekly")]
```

#### Test Terms Independently
##### Treatment
```{r pairwise-permanova-independent-treatment}
# set seed for permutations so that they are reproducible 
set.seed(100)

# Treatment model 
perm_pair_treatment <- pairwise.adonis2(y ~ Treatment, data = df_rates, method = "euclidean")

# put results into dataframe 
# list of comparisons
comparisons_treatment <- names(perm_pair_treatment)[2:4] #element 1 is the parent call which we don't need
# empty dataframe to put results in
df_PermPairTreatment <- data.frame()


for (i in 1:length(comparisons_treatment)) {
  # set counter as i + 1 in order to avoid grabbing parent call info from perm_pair_trial (element)
  counter <- i + 1
  
  # set comparison
  comparison <- comparisons_treatment[i]
  
  # grab first row of comparison model stats
  stats <- perm_pair_treatment[[counter]][1,]
  
  # combine comparison and stats into dataframe
  perm <- cbind(comparison, stats)
  
  # add perm dataframe to df_PermPairTrial dataframe 
  df_PermPairTreatment <- rbind(df_PermPairTreatment, perm)
}

# remove row names
rownames(df_PermPairTreatment) <- NULL
# rename p-value column
df_PermPairTreatment <- rename(df_PermPairTreatment, p = `Pr(>F)`)
# round numeric columns to 4 digits
df_PermPairTreatment <- df_PermPairTreatment %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, digits = 4))%>%
  add_column(term = "Treatment", .before = "comparison")

```
  
PBR vs Control: significant 
PBC vs Control: significant 
PBR vs PBC: not significant 

##### Trial
```{r pairwise-permanova-independent-trial}

# Trial model

# put results into dataframe

for (i in 1:length(comparisons_trial)) {

  # add perm dataframe to df_PermPairTrial dataframe

}

# remove row names

# rename p-value column

df_PermPairTrial <- df_PermPairTrial %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, digits = 4))%>%
  add_column(term = "Trial", .before = "comparison")

```

Experimental vs Control: 
  PBR 1 vs PBR 1 Control: not significant 
  PBC 1 vs PBC 1 Control: not significant 
  PBR 2 vs PBR 2 Control: significant 
  PBR 3 vs PBR 3 Control: not significant 
  PBC 2 vs PBC 2 Control: significant 
  PBC 3 vs PBC 3 Control: significant 

PBR vs PBC: 
  PBR 1 vs PBC 1: not significant 
  PBR 1 vs PBC 2: significant 
  PBR 1 vs PBC 3: significant 
  PBC 1 vs PBR 2: not significant 
  PBC 1 vs PBR 3: not significant 
  PBR 2 vs PBC 2: significant 
  PBR 2 vs PBC 3: significant 
  PBR 3 vs PBC 2: significant 
  PBR 3 vs PBC 3: significant 

PBR vs PBR: should be the same as each other -- and they are!
  PBR 1 vs PBR 2: not significant :)
  PBR 1 vs PBR 3: not significant :)
  PBR 2 vs PBR 3: not significant :)
  
PBC vs PBC: should be the same as each other -- and they are not :(
  *PBC 1 vs PBC 2: significant :(*
  *PBC 1 vs PBC 3: significant :(*
  *PBC 2 vs PBC 3: significant :(*
  
Control vs Control: all control trials should be the same as each other -- and they are not :(
  PBR 1 Control vs PBC 1 Control: not significant :)
  *PBR 1 Control vs PBC 2 Control: significant :(*
  *PBR 1 Control vs PBC 3 Control: significant :(*
  *PBC 1 Control vs PBR 2 Control: significant :(*
  PBC 1 Control vs PBR 3 Control: not significant :)
  *PBC 2 Control vs PBR 2 Control: significant :(*
  *PBC 2 Control vs PBR 3 Control: significant :(*
  PBR 3 Control vs PBC 3 Control: not significant :)
  
  *PBR 1 Control vs PBR 2 Control: significant :(*
  PBR 1 Control vs PBR 3 Control: not significant :)
  *PBR 2 Control vs PBR 3 Control: significant :(*

  *PBC 1 Control vs PBC 2 Control: significant :(*
  PBC 1 Control vs PBC 3 Control: not significant :)
  *PBC 2 Control vs PBC 3 Control: significant :(*
  

##### Species
```{r pairwise-permanova-independent-species}
# set seed for permutations so that they are reproducible 
set.seed(100)

# Species model
perm_pair_species <- pairwise.adonis2(y ~ Species, data = df_rates, method = "euclidean")

# put results into dataframe 
# list of comparisons
comparisons_species <- names(perm_pair_species)[2:4] #element 1 is the parent call which we don't need
# empty dataframe to put results in
df_PermPairSpecies <- data.frame()


for (i in 1:length(comparisons_species)) {
  # set counter as i + 1 in order to avoid grabbing parent call info from perm_pair_trial (element)
  counter <- i + 1
  
  # set comparison
  comparison <- comparisons_species[i]
  
  # grab first row of comparison model stats
  stats <- perm_pair_species[[counter]][1,]
  
  # combine comparison and stats into dataframe
  perm <- cbind(comparison, stats)
  
  # add perm dataframe to df_PermPairTrial dataframe 
  df_PermPairSpecies <- rbind(df_PermPairSpecies, perm)
}

# remove row names
rownames(df_PermPairSpecies) <- NULL
# rename p-value column
df_PermPairSpecies <- rename(df_PermPairSpecies, p = `Pr(>F)`)
# round numeric columns to 4 digits
df_PermPairSpecies <- df_PermPairSpecies %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, digits = 4)) %>%
  add_column(term = "Species", .before = "comparison")

```

Mcav vs Ofav: significant -- R^2 = 0.5
Mcav vs Pcli: not significant 
Ofav vs Pcli: significant  -- R^2 = 0.5

##### All Pairwise PERMANOVA Results 
```{r pairwise-permanova-results-all}
# combine all pairwise permanova results into one data frame
dfPairPermAll <- rbind(df_PermPairSpecies, df_PermPairTreatment, df_PermPairTrial, df_PermPairColony)

# write excel file of results
# write.xlsx(x = dfPairPermAll, file = "OutputData/StatisticsResults/MOStats_PERMANOVA_Pairwise_All.xlsx")

```


## Tukey Tests
For each of the 3 response variables, we are going to run Tukey's Honest Significant Difference (Tukey HSD) test on all 3 independent variables and their significant interactions from the single PERMANOVAs: Species, Trial, Treatment, Species:Treatment, and Species:Trial. 

### Data Set-Up
```{r post-hoc-tukey-data-setup}
# set up data frame for tukey testing 
df_rates_long <- df_rates %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = 5:7,
               names_to = "dependent_variable_names",
               values_to = "dependent_variable_values")

```

### Run Tukey Test
```{r tukey-test-treatment-species}
tukey_treat_tri_spec <- df_rates_long %>%
  group_by(dependent_variable_names) %>%
  tukey_hsd(dependent_variable_values ~ Treatment*Species*Trial) %>%
  select(-null.value) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, digits = 4)) 

# view results
tukey_treat_tri_spec

# make an excel file of results
# write.xlsx(x = tukey_treat_tri_spec, file = "OutputData/StatisticsResults/MOStats_TukeyTestResults.xlsx")

```

### Degrees of Freedom
#### Weight
```{r post-hoc-tukey-extra-stats}
summary(aov(weight_g_weekly ~ Treatment * Species * Trial, data = df_rates))
```
The degrees of freedom for a Tukey HSD test are the df of the Residuals from the ANOVA test that the Tukey test is based on, so 203 in this case.
